newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian budget not helping in poll - Oppn.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian budget not helping in poll - Oppn.

text.p: Australian opposition leader Kim Beazley said on Tuesday the government's harsh August budget was not helping Labor to win the Lindsay by-election to be held this Saturday, a party spokesman told reporters.
"It's a very tough task ahead of us," the spokesman quoted Beazley as saying.
"What assists the government there at the moment is the teeth of the budget are not really biting," Beazley said.
Australia's conservative government announced a tough budget for fiscal 1996/97 (July-June), slashing spending by A$3.9 billion to produce a forecast underlying deficit of A$5.6 billion.
Former minister Ross Free, who lost the Sydney-based seat in the March 2 election to the governing Liberal-National coalition, is Labor's candidate.
The High Court of Australia ordered the by-election after Liberal candidate Jackie Kelly was found inelligible under the constitution.
Kelly was found ineligible because she still received money from the government, as an airforce member and held Australian and New Zealand citizenship, both of which contravene the constitution.
